headline: Geometry is the mathematics of space—discovering eternal truths through shapes
universal_truth: The universe has structure; mathematics reveals patterns hidden in plain sight
fun_facts: Euclid's geometry textbook, written 2,300 years ago, is the second most reproduced book in history after the Bible
The angles of a triangle always sum to 180 degrees—this is true for any triangle anywhere
Non-Euclidean geometry—where parallel lines can meet—describes the curved space of our universe
discussion_questions: Why does geometry feel more 'certain' than other knowledge?
Where do you see geometric patterns in nature?
How does understanding shapes help in daily life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A circle is perfectly round everywhere. A triangle's angles always sum to 180 degrees. These aren't opinions or observations—they're mathematical certainties. Geometry discovers eternal truths written into the fabric of space itself.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Geometry gives us certainty in a way other subjects don't. When you prove a geometric theorem, it's true everywhere, forever. How is this possible? Where does this certainty come from?

options.text: Geometry derives conclusions logically from simple, self-evident starting points
options.response: Yes. From basic axioms, geometry builds chains of logic that guarantee conclusions. Pure reason, no observation needed.

options.text: Geometry describes physical reality, so it's as certain as the physical world
options.response: Geometry's certainty comes from logic, not observation—though it remarkably matches reality...

q1.title: Euclid's Gift
q1.script: Around 300 BCE, Euclid wrote 'Elements'—a geometry textbook that organized all known geometric knowledge into logical proofs from simple axioms. It taught logical thinking for 2,000 years and remains influential today.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Euclid's Gift"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Patterns Everywhere
q2.script: Geometry appears throughout nature: hexagonal honeycombs, spiral shells, branching trees. These aren't decorations—they're optimal solutions. Nature 'discovered' geometry through evolution, solving the same problems mathematicians study.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Flat
q3.script: Non-Euclidean geometry—where Euclid's rules don't apply—describes curved surfaces. On a sphere, triangle angles sum to more than 180 degrees. Einstein used this mathematics to describe how gravity curves space itself.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The universe has structure, and geometry reveals it. These aren't human inventions imposed on nature—they're patterns discovered within it. Mathematics is the language the universe is written in.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 105. Tomorrow, we'll explore how maps bend reality. Until then, notice geometric shapes around you—circles, squares, triangles—and appreciate the eternal patterns they embody.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Geometry Spotting - Find the Patterns
growTrack.learning_objective: Notice geometric patterns in the world
growTrack.activity: Look for geometric shapes today: circles in wheels and cups, rectangles in screens and doors, hexagons in nature. These patterns aren't accidental—they solve problems. What problems do the shapes you see solve?
